newsitem.title: UK: BT says talking with MCI on MCI outlook.
newsitem.headline: BT says talking with MCI on MCI outlook.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Thursday it was in talks with MCI Communications Corp on the change in outlook for MCI's results but that it would not have an impact on the companies' planned merger.
"BT has been notified by MCI management that the present outlook for MCI's results is worse than current market expectations," BT said in a statement.

"Initial discussions have been taking place with MCI management regarding this trading situation and BT will be holding further discussions with MCI management in order to fully understand the reasons for, and the extent of, the changes in MCI's prospects," BT said.

MCI announced in the U.S. earlier that it expected earnings for the second half 1997 and into 1998 to be below current Wall Street expectations due to delays in gaining entry into U.S. local phone service markets.
It said it expected earnings for the second quarter of 1997 to be in line with analysts' estimates.

BT and MCI are awaiting final regulatory approval for a planned $24 billion merger to be called Concert Plc. On Monday the deal was approved by the U.S. Justice Department but it still needs to be approved by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission.
A merger between the two British and American telecommunications giants would be the largest transAtlantic merger on record.

"It has nothing to do with the alliance," a BT spokesman said of MCI's changed outlook. "This is just an observation on the news MCI has given today. We're looking at the situation and talking to MCI about the background to it. That's all."
